disclaimer: Educational reference only. Never eat any wild plant, berry, or fungus based on an app. Confirm with a qualified local expert.

universal_rules.text: No wild mushroom is ever confirmed by an app; treat every mushroom ID as provisional until a qualified expert confirms it in person.
The so-called universal edibility test is a myth that kills; some deadly toxins take hours to act and are not detected by skin, lip, or tiny-taste steps.
White-gilled mushrooms with a ring on the stem and a cup at the base are treated as deadly Amanitas until proven otherwise.
Amatoxin poisoning has a deceptive 6–24 hour latent period where the victim feels better before liver failure begins.
Never eat anything with milky sap unless positively identified by an expert; many milky-sapped plants are toxic.
Umbellifers (carrot family) are off-limits without expert confirmation: water hemlock and poison hemlock kill in small amounts and resemble edible relatives.
Raw elderberry fruit, stems, leaves, and unripe fruit contain cyanogenic compounds; only cooked ripe fruit of verified species is used, and only with expert guidance.
Children and pets are at higher risk: smaller doses are dangerous, and attractive berries invite accidental ingestion. Supervise closely and teach no-taste rules.
Photograph the whole organism, fruit or cap close-up, leaves or gills, and growth habit before touching anything.
Wear gloves around contact hazards (poison ivy, hogweed, nettles), avoid touching face, and wash hands, tools, and clothing afterward.
Assess one specimen at a time; mixed patches and partial specimens cause the most dangerous misidentifications.
Cooking does not destroy amatoxins, many alkaloids, or cyanogenic compounds in pits and seeds; heat is not a safety test.
